## Finding the angle between vectors {#iv6-angle-formula .vector-lesson .magnitude-lesson .angles-lesson .a-formula}

```{=html}
<p>For two non-zero vectors in 2D or 3D:</p>
```

$$
\cos\theta=\frac{\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}}{|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|}
$$

```{=html}
<div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\boxed{\theta=\cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac{\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}}{|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|}\right)}"></span></div><div class="a-steps"><span>1. Scalar product</span><span>2. Magnitudes</span><span>3. Substitute and use inverse cosine</span></div><p>Measure from a common tail and report <span data-math="0^\circ\leq\theta\leq180^\circ"></span>. Use degree mode.</p>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet Section 6 · p. 41</div>

::: notes
Preserve exact square roots until the last step. A negative dot product gives an obtuse angle or 180°, so use the sign to check the result. The reflex angle gives the same cosine but is not the angle reported here. No repeated derivation from the cosine rule.
:::
